meta.title: The Kalman filter, derived and tested for consistency
meta.tools: Kalman filter as the linear minimum-variance estimator (own implementation), tracking an RC circuit's state and an unknown drifting input, NEES/NIS consistency tests, innovation whiteness, steady-state Riccati gain
meta.summary: Estimate the hidden states of a noisy second-order RC network from a single noisy voltage measurement, check that the filter's reported uncertainty is honest (normalised estimation error follows a χ² distribution), that innovations are white, and that the gain converges to the algebraic Riccati solution.
meta.problem: A filter that outputs a number and an error bar is only useful if the error bar is right. How do you prove a Kalman filter is consistent?
meta.theory:
For x_{k+1} = Ax_k + w, y_k = Cx_k + v: predict $P^- = APA^T + Q$, gain $K = P^-C^T(CP^-C^T+R)^{-1}$, update $P = (I-KC)P^-$ — derived by minimising E‖x − x̂‖² over linear estimators. Consistency: normalised estimation error
squared $ε = (x-\hat x)^TP^{-1}(x-\hat x)$ ~ χ²(n), innovations ν = y − Cx̂⁻ are white with variance CP⁻Cᵀ + R. P converges to the DARE solution regardless of initial P.
meta.method:
Two-node RC ladder (τ ≈ 1 ms, sampled at 10 kHz) plus a third state: the unknown input voltage modelled as a random walk. Process noise on all states, measurement noise σ = 20 mV on the output node.
100 Monte-Carlo runs × 2000 steps: average NEES vs χ² 95 % bounds, innovation autocorrelation, gain vs DARE.
